APH's AI Connectivity Growth Accelerates: Can It Outpace TEL & MRVL?
Mon, September 28, 2026 at 7:22 AM PDT 4 min read
Amphenol APH is benefiting from strong order momentum, improving operating leverage and robust profitability, strengthening its position across artificial intelligence (AI) data-center, communications and industrial connectivity markets. In the second quarter of 2026, orders grew 94% year over year and 14% sequentially to $10.7 billion, resulting in a book-to-bill ratio of 1.23:1. Every end market recorded a positive book-to-bill ratio, highlighting broad-based demand and improving revenue visibility. This momentum enhances APH's competitive positioning against Marvell Technology MRVL and TE Connectivity TEL.
Higher sales are also driving meaningful operating leverage. The adjusted operating margin expanded 420 basis points year over year and 250 basis points sequentially to 29.8%. Even excluding tariff recoveries, the margin approached 29%. CommScope contributed more than $1.2 billion in second-quarter sales and operated at a margin above 20%, including acquisition-related amortization. Management attributed the improvement to better factory execution, vendor management, SG&A discipline and leverage from higher volumes. Amphenol also raised its expected 2026 CommScope revenues to $4.6 billion from $4.1 billion, and doubled expected adjusted EPS accretion to 30 cents from 15 cents.
AI infrastructure remains a key growth driver. IT datacom represented 43% of second-quarter sales, with revenues rising 89% year over year and 63% organically. Sequential sales increased 22%, with virtually all growth driven by AI-related products. Amphenol is benefiting from demand for high-speed copper, fiber-optic and power interconnects, while CommScope is expanding its advanced optical presence. Strong execution is translating into higher earnings and cash flow. Adjusted EPS rose 67% year over year to $1.35, while operating and free cash flows reached $1.6 billion and $1.2 billion, respectively. APH ended the quarter with $8.4 billion of liquidity and a net leverage ratio of 1.3 times, supporting capacity expansion, product development and acquisitions.
Marvell Technology is challenging APH through rapid AI data-center growth and improving operating leverage. MRVL's second-quarter fiscal 2027 results raised the revenue outlook to roughly $12 billion, implying 45% growth, and lifted its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to $18 billion, representing nearly 50% growth. Data-center revenues are expected to rise 60% in fiscal 2027 and more than 60% in fiscal 2028, driven by strength across interconnect, switching and custom businesses. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, the non-GAAP operating margin was 36.6%, up 180 basis points year over year, demonstrating significant operating leverage in the business.
TE Connectivity is also pressuring APH through record orders and stronger profitability. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, the company reported record orders of $5.7 billion, up 27% year over year, while Digital Data Networks orders increased more than 70% from the start of the fiscal year to the end of the third quarter. TEL maintained a 1.1 book-to-bill ratio and ended the quarter with a record backlog. The adjusted operating margin expanded 90 basis points year over year to 21.9%, while management indicated that its industrial businesses can generate more than 30% flow-through at the current volume levels.

Investors might want to bet on TE Connectivity (TEL), as it has been recently upgraded to a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). This upgrade is essentially a reflection of an upward trend in earnings estimates -- one of the most powerful forces impacting stock prices.
The Zacks rating relies solely on a company's changing earnings picture. It tracks EPS estimates for the current and following years from the sell-side analysts covering the stock through a consensus measure -- the Zacks Consensus Estimate.
Since a changing earnings picture is a powerful factor influencing near-term stock price movements, the Zacks rating system is very useful for individual investors. They may find it difficult to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts, as these are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time.
As such, the Zacks rating upgrade for TE Connectivity is essentially a positive comment on its earnings outlook that could have a favorable impact on its stock price.
Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices
The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, and the near-term price movement of its stock are proven to be strongly correlated. That's partly because of the influence of institutional investors that use earnings and earnings estimates for calculating the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Their transaction of large amounts of shares then leads to price movement for the stock.
For TE Connectivity, rising earnings estimates and the consequent rating upgrade fundamentally mean an improvement in the company's underlying business. And investors' appreciation of this improving business trend should push the stock higher.
Harnessing the Power of Earnings Estimate Revisions

Here is where the tried-and-tested Zacks Rank stock-rating system plays an important role, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions.

APH's AI Datacom Strength Grows: Can It Challenge TEL & MRVL?
Amphenol APH is benefiting significantly from accelerating demand in the IT datacom market, particularly for artificial intelligence (AI)-related applications. In the second quarter of 2026, IT datacom represented 43% of APH's total sales, with revenues surging 89% year over year and 63% organically. Management also highlighted that the company's AI revenue run rate has reached roughly $10.5-$11 billion, with AI-related sales growing faster than the overall IT datacom business. This momentum is strengthening APH's position against TE Connectivity TEL and Marvell Technology MRVL in the expanding AI data-center connectivity market.
AI infrastructure expansion is driving strong demand for Amphenol's high-speed copper, fiber-optic and power interconnect solutions. Management noted that virtually all of the 22% sequential IT datacom growth in the second quarter of 2026 came from AI-related products. Customers are requiring more copper, optics and power as AI clusters grow larger and more complex. APH's portfolio spans passive and active fiber-optic solutions, high-speed copper and power connectivity, giving it exposure across multiple parts of the AI infrastructure stack. Power connectivity is another important growth opportunity.
APH's offerings include board-level power, bus bars and complex cable assemblies extending from chips and racks to data-center switchgear. Management highlighted higher-voltage architectures, liquid cooling and sensor-enabled power connectors as emerging opportunities. Rising power density in AI systems could therefore expand Amphenol's content per data center, complementing its high-speed data-connectivity business.
Amphenol's acquisition of CommScope is further strengthening its optical position. In the second quarter of 2026, CommScope contributed more than $1.2 billion in sales while adding significant fiber-optic interconnect capabilities for IT datacom. Management said CommScope's IT datacom business nearly doubled year over year and expects the market to account for just under half of CommScope's 2026 sales compared with roughly one-third in 2025. CommScope is participating in customer discussions around the potential introduction of optics into scale-up architectures.
APH's broad product portfolio may also help it participate across evolving AI architectures. Management said the company works with customers developing graphics processing unit, application-specific integrated circuit and XPU architectures, noting that all these architectures require interconnects. Management said inference is growing rapidly and requires an unprecedented level of interconnect intensity.
TE Connectivity remains a formidable competitor. outperforming end markets.
